questions.title: Which are combination reactions?
questions.text:
Which of the following are combination reactions?
(i) 2KClO₃ → 2KCl + 3O₂
(ii) MgO + H₂O → Mg(OH)₂
(iii) 4Al + 3O₂ → 2Al₂O₃
(iv) Zn + FeSO₄ → ZnSO₄ + Fe
opts: (i) and (iii)
(iii) and (iv)
(ii) and (iv)
(ii) and (iii)
steps: ① Combination: A + B → AB (one product)
② (i) one reactant → two products: decomposition
③ (ii) MgO + H₂O → Mg(OH)₂: one product ✓
④ (iii) 4Al + 3O₂ → 2Al₂O₃: one product ✓
⑤ (iv) Zn pushes Fe out: displacement
∴ (ii) and (iii) → (d)
questions.remember: Combination: two or more reactants form ONE product. Decomposition: ONE reactant breaks into two or more.
questions.trap: Picking (iii) and (iv): Zn + FeSO₄ has two products, so it is displacement, not combination.

questions.title: Electrolysis of water: the gas ratio
questions.text: The volume ratio of hydrogen and oxygen gases liberated during electrolysis of water is:
steps: ① Electricity splits water: decomposition
② 2H₂O → 2H₂ + O₂
③ 2 molecules of H₂ for every 1 of O₂
④ Equal molecules ⟹ equal volumes (same conditions)
questions.remember: Electrolysis of water: 2H₂O → 2H₂ + O₂. Hydrogen at the cathode, oxygen at the anode, volumes 2 : 1.
questions.trap: Picking 1 : 2 by reading the ratio as oxygen : hydrogen. The question asks hydrogen : oxygen.
questions.tryit: Which gas burns with a pop sound?

questions.title: Two white solids: which reaction type?
questions.text:
(i) AgNO₃ + NaCl → NaNO₃ + AgCl
(ii) K₂SO₄ + BaCl₂ → BaSO₄ + 2KCl
Which of the following options clearly describes both the reactions?
opts: (i) is double displacement, (ii) is displacement reaction.
Both (i) and (ii) are displacement reactions and precipitation reactions.
Both (i) and (ii) are double displacement reactions and precipitation reactions.
(i) is displacement, (ii) is double displacement reaction.
steps: ① (i) Ag and Na swap partners
② (ii) Ba and K swap partners
③ Ions exchanged in both ⟹ double displacement
④ AgCl and BaSO₄: insoluble white solids
⑤ Insoluble solid formed ⟹ precipitation
∴ Both: double displacement + precipitation → (c)
questions.ans: Option (c) Both are double displacement and precipitation reactions
questions.remember: Double displacement: two compounds exchange ions. If an insoluble solid forms, it is also a precipitation reaction.
questions.trap: Calling it 'displacement'. In displacement ONE element pushes another out; here TWO compounds swap ions.
questions.ncert: NCERT Ch 1 · Section 1.2.4 Double displacement reaction
questions.tryit: What colour is the BaSO₄ precipitate?

questions.title: Spot the displacement reaction
questions.text: Which of the following is an example of a displacement reaction?
opts: The combustion of natural gas
The reaction of a reactive metal with dilute acid
The electrolysis of water
The reaction of quick lime with water
steps: ① Displacement: a more reactive element pushes out a less reactive one
② Natural gas burning: CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O ✗
③ Electrolysis: 2H₂O → 2H₂ + O₂ ⟹ decomposition ✗
④ Quick lime: CaO + H₂O → Ca(OH)₂ ⟹ combination ✗
⑤ Zn + H₂SO₄ → ZnSO₄ + H₂ ⟹ Zn pushes H out ✓
∴ Reactive metal + dilute acid → (b)
questions.ans: Option (b) The reaction of a reactive metal with dilute acid
questions.remember: Displacement: A + BC → AC + B, where A is more reactive than B. A reactive metal displaces hydrogen from a dilute acid.
questions.trap: Picking quick lime and water. CaO + H₂O → Ca(OH)₂ makes ONE product: combination.
questions.tryit: Fe + CuSO₄ → FeSO₄ + Cu: which type?

questions.title: Heating green ferrous sulphate
questions.text: When ferrous sulphate crystals are heated in a test tube, we observe that:
opts: A colourless gas with no smell is evolved.
A brown gas is evolved.
The green colour of the salt fades and a gas with the smell of burning sulphur is evolved.
The green colour of the salt fades and no gas is evolved.
steps: ① FeSO₄ crystals are green (they hold water)
② On heating, the water leaves ⟹ green fades
③ 2FeSO₄ → Fe₂O₃ + SO₂ + SO₃
④ SO₂ and SO₃ smell of burning sulphur
∴ Green fades + burning-sulphur smell → (c)
questions.ans: Option (c) The green colour fades and a gas with the smell of burning sulphur is evolved
questions.remember: 2FeSO₄ → Fe₂O₃ + SO₂ + SO₃ (thermal decomposition). Green crystals lose colour; the gases smell of burning sulphur.
questions.trap: Picking 'a brown gas'. Brown fumes (NO₂) come from heating lead nitrate, not ferrous sulphate.
questions.tryit: What is the solid left behind, and its colour?

questions.title: Heating lead nitrate: which gases?
questions.text: The gases evolved on heating lead (II) nitrate crystals are:
opts: NO and O₂
N₂ and NO₂
NO₂ and H₂
NO₂ and O₂
steps: ① 2Pb(NO₃)₂ → 2PbO + 4NO₂ + O₂
② Brown fumes = NO₂ (nitrogen dioxide)
③ Oxygen is given off too
④ No hydrogen in lead nitrate ⟹ (c) impossible
∴ NO₂ and O₂ → (d)
questions.remember: 2Pb(NO₃)₂ → 2PbO + 4NO₂ + O₂: brown fumes of nitrogen dioxide, plus oxygen. Thermal decomposition.
questions.trap: Picking NO (nitric oxide). The brown gas is NO₂, nitrogen DIoxide.
questions.tryit: What colour is the lead oxide left behind?

questions.title: Silver jewellery turning black
questions.text: A student notices that her silver jewellery turned dull and had a grey-black coating over it after wearing for a few months. What results in the change in colour of the silver metal?
opts: The polish over the jewellery was removed after wearing for a few months.
The jewellery comes in contact with air, moisture and acids and corrodes.
Dust particles over the jewellery change its colour.
Its colour changes due to rusting.
steps: ① Silver reacts with sulphur compounds in air
② The black coating is silver sulphide, Ag₂S
③ A metal attacked by air, moisture, acids ⟹ corrosion
④ Rusting is ONLY for iron ⟹ (d) ✗
∴ Corrosion → (b)
questions.ans: Option (b) It comes in contact with air, moisture and acids and corrodes
questions.remember: Corrosion: a metal attacked by air, moisture or acids. Silver turns black (Ag₂S), copper turns green; iron's corrosion is called rusting.
questions.trap: Picking 'rusting'. Rusting is the word ONLY for iron; silver tarnishes (corrodes).
questions.tryit: What coating forms on copper left in moist air?

questions.title: Oxidised, reduced, and a quick balance
questions.text:
(a) Name the substance oxidised and reduced in the following reaction:
ZnO + C → Zn + CO
(b) Balance the following chemical reaction:
Pb(NO₃)₂ + KI → PbI₂ + KNO₃
(c) Give one example each of electrolytic decomposition and decomposition by sunlight.
steps: ① (a) ZnO loses oxygen ⟹ ZnO is reduced
② C gains oxygen ⟹ C is oxidised
③ (b) Right side has 2 I and 2 NO₃ ⟹ 2KI, 2KNO₃
④ Pb(NO₃)₂ + 2KI → PbI₂ + 2KNO₃
⑤ (c) Electricity: 2H₂O → 2H₂ + O₂
⑥ Sunlight: 2AgCl → 2Ag + Cl₂
∴ C oxidised, ZnO reduced; balanced; 2 examples
questions.ans: (a) Oxidised: C · Reduced: ZnO   (b) Pb(NO₃)₂ + 2KI → PbI₂ + 2KNO₃   (c) 2H₂O → 2H₂ + O₂; 2AgCl → 2Ag + Cl₂
questions.remember: Gain of oxygen = oxidation; loss of oxygen = reduction. Balance by counting each atom (or ion group like NO₃) on both sides.
questions.trap: (a): saying Zn is oxidised. Zinc is the PRODUCT; it's ZnO that loses oxygen (reduced) and C that gains it (oxidised).
questions.tryit: CuO + H₂ → Cu + H₂O: which is oxidised?
questions.tryans: H₂ is oxidised (gains O); CuO is reduced

questions.title: Copper heated in air, then in hydrogen
questions.text: Seema took a small amount of copper powder in a china dish and heated it. What changes will she observe on heating? When H₂ gas is passed over this heated substance, what visible changes will be seen in it? Give the chemical equations of the reactions involved, along with the names and colours of the products in each case.
steps: ① Brown copper turns black on heating
② 2Cu + O₂ → 2CuO (copper(II) oxide, black)
③ Copper gains oxygen ⟹ oxidation
④ H₂ over hot CuO: black turns brown again
⑤ CuO + H₂ → Cu + H₂O (copper, brown; water)
∴ Black CuO, then brown Cu + water drops
questions.ans: 2Cu + O₂ → 2CuO (black copper(II) oxide); CuO + H₂ → Cu + H₂O (brown copper and water)
questions.remember: 2Cu + O₂ → 2CuO: brown → black (oxidation). CuO + H₂ → Cu + H₂O: black → brown (CuO reduced, H₂ oxidised).
questions.trap: Forgetting the colours or names of the products: the question asks for both, and they carry the marks.
questions.tryit: In CuO + H₂ → Cu + H₂O, what is the oxidising agent?

questions.title: Give reasons: chips, breathing, dark bottles
questions.text:
Give reasons:
(i) Potato chips manufacturers fill the packet of chips with nitrogen gas.
(ii) Respiration is an exothermic reaction.
(iii) Silver chloride is stored in dark coloured bottles.
steps: ① (i) Oxygen oxidises fats and oils ⟹ rancid
② Nitrogen is unreactive ⟹ no oxidation, no rancidity
③ (ii) Glucose is oxidised in our cells
④ C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ → 6CO₂ + 6H₂O + energy
⑤ (iii) Light decomposes silver chloride
⑥ 2AgCl → 2Ag + Cl₂ (sunlight)
∴ Stop rancidity · energy released · block light
questions.ans: (i) N₂ prevents oxidation (rancidity) · (ii) glucose is oxidised, releasing energy · (iii) light decomposes AgCl
questions.remember: Rancidity: oxidation of fats and oils (prevented by N₂, airtight packing, antioxidants). Respiration releases energy: exothermic.
questions.trap: (i): writing 'nitrogen keeps chips crispy'. The marking point is that it PREVENTS OXIDATION / rancidity.
questions.tryit: Name one more way to slow down rancidity.
questions.tryans: Airtight containers, refrigeration, or adding antioxidants
